major_events: Zhou Mingrui transmigrates into Klein Moretti, finding a self-inflicted gunshot wound
Klein activates the 'Fortune Transference Ritual' and discovers the gray fog world
The Tarot Club is founded with 'Justice' (Audrey Hall) and 'Hanged Man' (Alger Wilson)
Klein joins the Nighthawks (Blackthorn Security) after the Antigonus notebook incident
The pursuit, battle, and sealing of the Antigonus family notebook and Marionettist 2-049
Klein becomes Sequence 8 Clown after digesting the Seer potion via the Acting Method
The corruption and death of Neil due to the Hidden Sage's influence
The interception of the True Creator's child ritual involving Mehaose and Lanevus
Captain Dunn's sacrifice to suppress the entity using Saint Selena's ashes
Klein is killed by Ince Zangwill, who steals the saint's ashes to advance to Sequence 4
Klein resurrects from his grave, swears vengeance, and relocates to Backlund
He adopts the alias Sherlock Moriarty and registers as a private detective
The Tarot Club learns the 'Beyonder Characteristic Non-Convergence Law'
The identity and capabilities of Sealed Artifact 0-08 (Quill of Alzur) are inferred
Klein navigates Backlund's underworld, encountering its social strata and pollution
The fate of the 'Monster' Ademisaul and the lingering web of Ince's manipulation
character_state_transitions: Zhou Mingrui → Klein Moretti (soul replacement, amnesia fused with native body)
Klein: Ordinary graduate → Sequence 9 Seer → Sequence 8 Clown
Dunn Smith: Competent captain → Grieving, corrupted leader → Sacrificed protector
Leonard Mitchell: Cynical poet → Bereaved, vengeful Nighthawk (joins Red Gloves)
Old Neil: Mentor arcana-practitioner → Corrupted by Hidden Sage → Executed by teammates
Audrey Hall: Innocent debutante → Disciplined 'Audience' → Mature 'Justice'
Alger Wilson: Lone sailor → 'Hanged Man' acolyte → Ambitious 'Admiral' figure
Trissy: Powerful 'Assassin'/Instigator → Female 'Witch' → Escaped, sealed threat
Sharron: Hostile Marionettist → Reluctant collaborator → Autonomous sealed entity
long_form_mechanisms: Acting Method: digesting potions by behaving as the sequence title demands
Ritual Magic: invoking deities (Evernight Goddess) with precise herb/symbol arrangements
Divination: spirit vision, pendulum (confirm/deny), coin-toss (boundary guess), dream divination
Sealed Artifact hierarchy: 0 (world-ending) → 1 → 2 → 3 (lowest), with containment procedures
Tarot Club exchange system: encrypted prayer-requests, gray-fog interpretation, escrow trade
Beyonder pathways: sequences 1–9 each bestow unique abilities; high-sequence convergence possible
Characteristic non-annihilation law: traits persist and transfer (key to potion/ingredient logic)
Gray Fog platform: chrono-spatial hub for cross-continent communication and isolation
continuity_observations: Ince Zangwill's Quill of Alzur repeatedly writes 'coincidences' that push the plot (e.g., Klein finding the notebook, Dunn's corruption deepening)
The Antigonus notebook's curse is never fully neutralized; it attracts the Nighthawks, the Secret Order, and the Aurora Order in overlapping arcs
Klein's transmigration ritual consistently works only through the gray fog; the 'Fortune God' incantation remains a fixed anchor
Dunn's memory lapses and impulsive decisions (e.g., failing to retreat into the Chanis Gate) are subtle signs of notebook-caused spiritual pollution
The theme of manufacturing sacrifice (factory pollution, dead workers) builds a consistent critique of the industrial-capitalist backdrop
Every Tarot Club meeting yields new diary fragments of Emperor Roselle, each advancing the world's hidden cosmology
The 'Hornacis' whisper appears each time the Antigonus legacy awakens; Klein's resistance reflects his unique gray-fog connection
Old Neil's corruption by the Hidden Sage parallels the broader 'failed resurrection' motif (e.g., the Countess's portrait, the ghost knight)
style_observations: Descending exposition: the isekai framework explains the world slowly (clothes, coins, gas lamps) before bursting into action
Pseudo-Victorian mise-en-scène: gaslights, tailcoats, hansom cabs, newspapers, and a layered class society
Hybrid occult-system: tarot cards, Western astrology, and Chinese Xianxia cultivation cores fuse into a single ladder of sequences
Sudden tonal collapse: mundane domestic scenes (cooking, sister banter) interrupt cosmic horror, amplifying the dread
Tarot Club as narrative scaffold: every third chapter resets the world-map through dialogue, allowing parallel plotlines to breathe
Roselle's diary as metafiction: Roselle's authorial complaints foreshadow future mechanics, letting the author comment on his own story within the story

creation_family_evidence.author: 爱潜水的乌贼
creation_family_evidence.novel_series_context: First complete novel of the 'Lord of the Mysteries' series (6–8 planned volumes)
creation_family_evidence.cultural_reference_cluster: H. P. Lovecraft mythos, Victorian economics (Factory Acts), tarot occultism, and Jin Yong's chivalric integrity

originality_risks: 'Transmigrator gains meta-knowledge of the Acting Method' closely mirrors power-fantasy system novels, risking immersion collapse
The Tarot Club assembly model resembles MMO guild mechanics (gather, vote, exchange) more than clandestine cabal realism
Victorian London repacked with Chinese web-novel flavor may read as derivative despite novel execution—the 'familiar exotic'
The 'divination tells everything' mechanic could trivialize tension if the cost (spiritual exhaustion) is not enforced rigorously
